name: digital learning resource quality evaluation framework
description: Background Digital learning resources (DLRs) are now core teaching tools in health professions education, yet quality evaluation remains constrained by subjective weighting bias and a persistent gap between educational importance and operational measurability. Because DLRs increasingly mediate what and how students learn, deficiencies in resource quality propagate directly into competency attainment, making quality evaluation a proximal determinant of student competency outcomes. This study aimed to develop and validate a practical DLR quality evaluation framework for medical and public health education. Methods A sequential mixed-methods design was employed. First, a modified Delphi procedure with 26 experts was used to construct the hierarchical indicator system. Second, an expert-based and data-derived integrated weighting model combining AHP and EWM was developed to balance expert judgment and data discriminatory power. Third, a measurability correction mechanism and a four-quadrant prioritization matrix were established. The framework was validated with 10 DLRs across 10 medical courses, involving 309 students. Results The final system comprised 4 primary dimensions, 9 secondary indicators, and 14 tertiary indicators. Content Quality had the highest integrated weight (0.469), with Data Visualization (0.136) and Updated Content and Frontier Knowledge (0.103) as the top tertiary indicators.
